title: Data centers become 'killer application' for new power transformer tech
summary: The rapid growth of AI data centers is driving demand for solid-state power transformers, a modern alternative to conventional transformers. These new transformers use semiconductor technology to improve efficiency, reduce size, and enable mass production, addressing supply chain bottlenecks and supporting DC power architectures favored by AI data centers. Their modular design and ability to handle AC/DC conversion in a single device make them ideal for data centers and electric vehicle charging, with potential broader applications in power grids and homes.
key_points: AI data centers are the primary driver for adopting solid-state power transformers, which replace century-old conventional transformer technology.
Conventional transformers are hand-assembled, custom-built, and face long lead times (years) due to manufacturing constraints, hindering power grid expansion.
Solid-state transformers use high-frequency semiconductor switching (e.g., silicon carbide) for voltage conversion, enabling mass production and modular designs.
They are smaller, lighter, and can directly convert AC to DC power, eliminating the need for separate conversion devices in data centers.
Companies like Amperesand, Heron Power, and DG Matrix have raised over $280 million to commercialize this technology.
Solid-state transformers reduce material usage (e.g., copper) and physical footprint, offering flexibility for data center design.
They could alleviate supply chain shortages for power transformers, benefiting broader grid upgrades beyond data centers.
The technology is also applicable to electric vehicle charging, where DC power is essential, and could enable DC power distribution in homes.
A recent demonstration by North Carolina State University showed a solid-state transformer handling 1 MW of power for EV charging, proving its viability.
Challenges remain in engineering and commercialization, but data center adoption may accelerate broader market acceptance.
